unit: Algebra · Chapter 3. Logic; sequences and limits
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 11 mathematics textbooks (general stream)

stages.headline: A sequence assigns a number aₙ to every natural n; it is given by a formula for the general term or by a recurrence.
stages.headlineEnglish: A sequence assigns a number aₙ to every natural n; it is given by a formula for the general term or by a recurrence.

stages.headline: A sequence is increasing if aₙ₊₁ > aₙ and decreasing if aₙ₊₁ < aₙ for every n; aₙ = 1/n is decreasing.
stages.headlineEnglish: A sequence is increasing if aₙ₊₁ > aₙ and decreasing if aₙ₊₁ < aₙ for every n; aₙ = 1/n is decreasing.

stages.headline: A sequence is bounded if |aₙ| ≤ M for some M and every n: aₙ = (−1)ⁿ is bounded (M = 1), aₙ = n² is not.
stages.headlineEnglish: A sequence is bounded if |aₙ| ≤ M for some M and every n: aₙ = (−1)ⁿ is bounded (M = 1), aₙ = n² is not.
